mathematical_audit.exact_decomposition: For S=A+5B/2 and D_m=2lambda_1-5lambda_0, every polynomial combination is exactly S(m)lambda_0,m+B(m)D_m/2. Item420 gives D_m=m^-1 CT(qH^m), so the two summands differ by one power of m at the same exponential phase.
mathematical_audit.critical_ratio: At a dominant saddle alpha, the ratio of the post-integration amplitude to the original one is t(alpha)=q(alpha)/f_0(alpha). Exact elimination gives 320t^3-400t^2+220t-11, with discriminant -3460300800. The numerator and denominator resultants 176 and 5120 exclude zero or pole values. The real critical point maps to the unique real root, so the conjugate dominant saddles map to the nonreal conjugate roots.
mathematical_audit.degree_comparison: If deg S differs from deg B-1, one saddle contribution has strictly larger polynomial scale and a nonzero amplitude. In the tie deg S=deg B-1, rational real leading coefficients would require a real multiple of the nonreal t(alpha) to cancel, which is impossible.
mathematical_audit.limsup: Every nonzero pair therefore has a nonzero two-conjugate-saddle leading term at root rho_*. Cesaro averaging of cos^2 supplies an infinite noncancelling subsequence; polynomial powers do not affect m-th roots, proving the limsup without a pointwise lower bound.
mathematical_audit.normalization: A fixed denominator clears A and B without exponential cost, and log F_m=C_F m+o(m). Division by F_m therefore changes the root to rho_* exp(-C_F)=13.1004071782333102143....
mathematical_audit.scope: The theorem concerns one same-index fixed-degree polynomial-in-m combination bounded by ordinary absolute height. It does not bound the joint gcd, shifted-row recurrences, growing degree, adaptive modular coefficients, or two-combination resultants.
